visual.glance_promise: Before you escalate a supply risk: an illustrative four-gate customer-first check.
visual.primary_reading_route: changed supplier date -> date reliability -> customer exposure -> recovery check -> joint exception -> meeting question

core_units.visual_teaches: A date signal needs validation before it becomes a customer-facing promise.

core_units.on_visual_text: Can any credible date miss need-by?
core_units.visual_teaches: Supplier-date reliability and customer exposure are separate gates.
A proposed recovery option must be checked before it becomes a promised result.
The unresolved customer exception receives named joint ownership in this proposed method.

caption.job: Explain why teams collapse different unknowns into one ‘supply risk,’ restate the non-predictive boundary, and ask a discussion question. Do not narrate the four gate labels or supporting instructions.
adds: Why a changed confirmation is not automatically a customer exception.
The cost of manufactured certainty and premature cost optimisation.
A question that surfaces the fact still missing from the meeting.
must_not_repeat: The four gate titles or their explanatory sentences.

hook.job: Name the unresolved customer-exception moment without summarising the four gates.
hook.why_this_mode: The first line is recognisable and leaves the visual to make the operating distinction legible.

review.notes: The caption uses the idea of validation and exception ownership but does not duplicate a complete visual-unit label or its instruction.
